name: Plain HTTPS resolved via DNS
note: Control case. If this is missing, nothing else in the run is trustworthy.

name: HTTPS straight to an IP, no DNS lookup
note: iptables redirects on port, not on having resolved a name, so skipping DNS does not skip the proxy. host_is_ip discriminates this from the hostname control case — without it, the control satisfied this case and the suite could not fail even if direct-to-IP interception broke. Also covers DNS-over-HTTPS, which is indistinguishable from any other HTTPS request to a resolver's IP.

name: DNS-over-TLS on port 853
note: Logged via conntrack in monitor mode; rejected outright by the enforce-mode rules.

name: QUIC / UDP on port 443
note: HTTP/3 bypasses a TCP-only proxy, so UDP 443 is logged in monitor mode and rejected in enforce. Regression-guards the transport-aware dedup fix — this was silently dropped as a duplicate of TCP 443 to the same host.

name: Raw TCP on a non-standard port
note: Outside the 80/443 redirect, so visibility comes from conntrack logging rather than the proxy.

name: DNS query
note: The DNS interceptor is the only leg that sees a name before anything connects.

name: Egress from a process running as the proxy user
note: KNOWN GAP. The redirect carries `! --uid-owner pipewardenuser` so the proxy does not intercept itself, which exempts anything able to run as that user. Requires sudo, which a compromised build step on a GitHub-hosted runner already has.
